newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury warns against citizens' control of IRS.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury warns against citizens' control of IRS.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers sharply criticized a proposal to remove control of the tax-collecting Internal Revenue Service from the executive branch and to put a board of citizens in charge.

"The ability to collect taxes lies at the heart of the notion of sovereignty and the legitimacy of government," Summers said in a speech prepared for delivery to the American Institute of Certified Accountants.
Summers said a proposal for citizen control of the IRS, rather than having the agency come under Treasury as it now does, was "dangerously flawed" and raised serious concerns.

The current arrangement puts accountability for the IRS on the Treasury Secretary and the Deputy Treasury Secretary, Summers, adding that was preferable to spreading the responsibility across an unelected committee.

Summers said the IRS "cannot be run like a private company." There was a potential for conflicts of interest if a board of citizens ran it, Summers suggested, as well as possible law enforcement issues that might lead to constitutional challenges.
"The very notion of private citizens charged with enforcing the nation's laws would undoubtedly be unacceptable to the public," Summers said.

He warned that with reform efforts already under way to make the tax-collecting agency more efficient, the possibility of a public debate on how the IRS should be governed "risks paralysis at the very moment when we have begun to make progress."
